title: Hidden Global State Dependency in Constructor
pattern: A struct constructor (`new` or equivalent builder) directly accesses a global singleton or lazy-static context variable to resolve its configuration.
why_bad: The dependency on the global is hidden. A developer looking at `Connection::new()` cannot tell that it depends on global configuration. It makes testing impossible without setting up the global state beforehand.
detection: Accessing global variables or singleton registry structures inside standard constructors or initialization methods.
counterexample: Framework-level dependency injectors that explicitly annotate and manage construction lifetimes, though manual constructor injection is still safer.
source: Michael Feathers, *Working Effectively with Legacy Code* (2004), Chapter 14 ("Dependencies on Globals"); Andrew Hunt & David Thomas, *The Pragmatic Programmer* (2019), Chapter 2 ("Globalization").
